prompt: Which of these is a symptom rather than a mood?

choices.text: the fan runs, the light comes on, the screen stays black
choices.why: Specific enough that two people would agree it happened.

choices.text: the computer is not working properly any more
choices.why: That covers a hundred different faults at once.

choices.text: something seems to be wrong with the hardware
choices.why: That is a guess at the cause wearing a description.

choices.text: the whole machine has become completely unusable since then
choices.why: A conclusion about severity, and not a description.

prompt: Why does the lesson call a symptom that happens sometimes valuable?

choices.text: an intermittent fault is easier to reproduce on demand
choices.why: It is the hardest kind to reproduce.

choices.text: it means the hardware is probably still under warranty
choices.why: Warranties have nothing to do with it.

choices.text: a fault that comes and goes tends to fix itself
choices.why: Nothing here fixes itself.

choices.text: the pattern of when it happens narrows the cause
choices.why: Every Tuesday morning is already an enormous clue.

prompt: What is the answer to "what changed", and why does it matter?

choices.text: nothing, and that genuinely rules out recent changes
choices.why: It rules out only what the person noticed.

choices.text: an update, which is the cause in most cases
choices.why: Often a cause, and not something to assume.

choices.text: nothing, and it is very nearly always wrong
choices.why: An update, a cable moved, somebody else on the machine.

choices.text: a list of changes, which people keep reliably
choices.why: Almost nobody keeps one.

prompt: Why is reproducing the fault most of the job?

choices.text: it is what a support line asks for before helping
choices.why: Sometimes true, and not the reason.

choices.text: without it, every change appears to have worked
choices.why: The fault has simply not happened yet.

choices.text: repeating it makes the underlying cause visible
choices.why: It makes testing possible, which is different.

choices.text: a fault that repeats is always a hardware fault
choices.why: Software repeats perfectly well.

prompt: "The hard disk is failing" — what is wrong with that as a report?

choices.text: it is a conclusion, and it ends the investigation
choices.why: The symptom was thirty-second opens and a clicking noise.

choices.text: it names a part rather than the whole machine
choices.why: Naming a part is fine when it was tested.

choices.text: it is too technical for a person to have observed
choices.why: People say it constantly.

choices.text: it gives no indication of how old the disk is
choices.why: Age is a detail, and not the problem here.

prompt: Which fact shrinks the search the most, and is usually left out?

choices.text: how urgent the person says the problem is
choices.why: That changes your order, not the cause.

choices.text: how long the person has owned the machine
choices.why: Rarely decides anything.

choices.text: the make and the model of the machine
choices.why: Useful later, and it narrows little.

choices.text: the list of things that still work
choices.why: Everything is broken is almost never true.

prompt: Before changing anything, find the shortest sequence that ___ the fault.
What does halving buy that checking one at a time does not?

choices.text: it works on hardware faults and not software ones
choices.why: It is indifferent to both.

choices.text: every test removes a half, whether it passes or fails
choices.why: So no test is wasted.

choices.text: it finds the fault on the very first attempt more often
choices.why: It is not about being lucky earlier.

choices.text: it needs no knowledge of what the chain contains
choices.why: Knowing the chain is the hard part.

prompt: Eight links checked one at a time is up to eight tests. Halved?

choices.text: four
choices.why: That is sixteen links.

choices.text: three
choices.why: Eight, four, two, one.

choices.text: two
choices.why: Two tests only settle four links.

choices.text: six
choices.why: Halving does not work like that.

prompt: A document will not print. Where is the middle of that chain?

choices.text: the printer, tested by switching it off and on again
choices.why: That is one end, and it is a remedy.

choices.text: the print queue, tested from another application
choices.why: One test, and half the chain is gone.

choices.text: the driver, reinstalled just to be certain about it
choices.why: A change rather than a test, and not the middle.

choices.text: the document, tested by opening it again
choices.why: That is the other end.

prompt: A machine will not start. What is the halving test?

choices.text: is the power cable seated firmly in the socket
choices.why: One end of the chain.

choices.text: does the screen show the maker logo briefly
choices.why: Useful, and it is far down one half.

choices.text: has the machine been dropped in the last week
choices.why: A history question, not a test.

choices.text: does anything at all light up or spin
choices.why: It separates two halves with nothing in common.

prompt: Why is the mathematical middle not always where to cut?

choices.text: chains in practice have an even number of links
choices.why: That changes nothing here.

choices.text: the two halves are rarely the same size anyway
choices.why: True, and it is not the reason.

choices.text: the middle link is usually the least likely cause
choices.why: Likelihood is not what halving uses.

choices.text: a cheap test off-centre beats an expensive one in the middle
choices.why: Cut at a joint you can actually reach.

prompt: What is wrong with fixing the most likely cause first?

choices.text: it requires knowledge the person does not have
choices.why: It requires exactly the knowledge people do have.

choices.text: it cannot be combined with any other method
choices.why: It combines fine; it just does not narrow.

choices.text: being wrong three times leaves you where you began
choices.why: It is fast when right and has no structure.

choices.text: the most likely cause is almost never the real one
choices.why: It often is, which is why the habit survives.

prompt: Match each fault to the test that cuts its chain in half.

pairs.right: look for any light or fan at all
run it in a second account

prompt: Two changes made together, and it works. What do you know?

choices.text: that the fault was in whatever the two had in common
choices.why: They may have nothing in common.

choices.text: that both changes were needed to fix it
choices.why: One of four possibilities.

choices.text: nothing that helps, since four explanations remain
choices.why: Either one, both, or neither and something else moved.

choices.text: that the second change is the one that really mattered
choices.why: There is no reason to think so.

prompt: Which clause of the rule does everybody drop?

choices.text: put it back if it did not help
choices.why: Left in place, it becomes part of the next fault.

choices.text: test after every change you make
choices.why: Skipped less often than the third.

choices.text: write down what you expected to happen
choices.why: Part of the note, and not the rule itself.

choices.text: change only one thing at a time
choices.why: Everybody knows this one and most try.

prompt: Why is a change left in place worse than it looks?

choices.text: it slowly degrades the performance of the machine
choices.why: Most settings cost nothing.

choices.text: it makes the machine harder to sell later on
choices.why: Not the concern here.

choices.text: next time it is in the "nothing changed" answer
choices.why: And it will be believed.

choices.text: it prevents the system from updating itself
choices.why: Nothing like that follows.

prompt: What specifically does the written note prevent?

choices.text: making the same mistake on a different machine
choices.why: A benefit, and not the one named.

choices.text: going back to something already tried and forgotten
choices.why: That loop eats an evening and feels like progress.

choices.text: having to restart the whole investigation later
choices.why: It helps, and the named failure is the loop.

choices.text: being blamed for a change somebody else made
choices.why: Not what it is for.

prompt: Which of these keep a change undoable?

choices.text: disconnecting a device rather than reconfiguring it
choices.why: Plugging it back in is the whole undo.

choices.text: applying every change at once to save restarts
choices.why: That is the opposite of the rule.

choices.text: preferring a setting to an installation
choices.why: A setting goes back; an installation leaves traces.

choices.text: copying a configuration file before editing it
choices.why: The copy is the undo.

prompt: Why does the lesson call an irreversible change dangerous?

choices.text: it cannot be described in a written note
choices.why: It can be written down perfectly well.

choices.text: it tends to be the change that causes the fault
choices.why: No more than any other.

choices.text: it usually voids the warranty on the hardware
choices.why: A real cost, and not this argument.

choices.text: from then on every test runs on a different machine
choices.why: A variable became permanent.

prompt: Change one thing, test, and if it did not help, ___ it back.
What is the one-sentence rule of substitution?

choices.text: the symptom follows the faulty part
choices.why: Which way it goes is the answer.

choices.text: the cheaper part is the one to replace first
choices.why: That is a shopping rule, not a test.

choices.text: a part that was moved recently is the suspect
choices.why: A hypothesis, and not what a swap proves.

choices.text: two identical parts fail in the same way
choices.why: They do not, and it proves nothing.

prompt: A black monitor works on a second machine. What does that settle?

choices.text: the cable on the second machine is the good one
choices.why: That is the swap, and not the conclusion.

choices.text: the monitor is fine, and the fault is behind it
choices.why: The machine or the cable it was on.

choices.text: the second machine has a different graphics card
choices.why: True, and it settles nothing.

choices.text: the monitor is faulty and intermittently so
choices.why: It just worked.

prompt: What does a swap prove?

choices.text: that the replacement part is in good condition
choices.why: That has to be known beforehand.

choices.text: whether the fault is hardware or software
choices.why: Sometimes, and it is not the general claim.

choices.text: what the fault is, once the part is identified
choices.why: The part is identified; the fault is not.

choices.text: where the fault is, and never what it is
choices.why: Panel, supply or board inside is a further question.

prompt: Why is "a second cable from the same drawer" a bad swap?

choices.text: it is different rather than known to be good
choices.why: Both have been in the drawer the same ten years.

choices.text: a cable is almost never the cause of a fault
choices.why: A cable is the highest-yield swap there is.

choices.text: two cables of the same type behave identically
choices.why: They do not, which is why the swap tempts.

choices.text: the drawer cable is likely to be the wrong standard
choices.why: A separate problem, if it happens.

prompt: What is safe mode a swap of?

choices.text: the hardware, for a minimal set of components
choices.why: The hardware is untouched.

choices.text: the whole system, for a copy on a stick
choices.why: That is the live stick, and it is another test.

choices.text: everything added since the machine was new
choices.why: Drivers, startup programs, installed things.

choices.text: the user account, for a fresh empty one
choices.why: That is a different test.

prompt: The fault happens in safe mode too. What follows?

choices.text: the test was inconclusive and must be repeated
choices.why: It was conclusive, and in the other direction.

choices.text: it is the hardware or the system, not something added
choices.why: Uninstalling things will not help.

choices.text: a startup program is loading in safe mode as well as normally
choices.why: Safe mode is what stops them.

choices.text: the machine needs to be reinstalled from scratch
choices.why: That is a remedy for one of the two.

prompt: There is nothing to swap with. What does the lesson suggest?

choices.text: buy the part that seems most likely to be faulty
choices.why: That is a guess with a receipt.

choices.text: ask what you would need to borrow to settle it
choices.why: The answer shows what you actually suspect.

choices.text: assume the oldest component is the faulty one
choices.why: Age is not evidence.

choices.text: treat the swap as done and move on regardless
choices.why: That records a guess as a test.

prompt: Why is "did it ever work" the first question?

choices.text: people answer it more honestly than the others
choices.why: People rarely volunteer it at all.

choices.text: it tells you roughly how old the equipment is
choices.why: Age is not what it buys.

choices.text: never worked and stopped working are different searches
choices.why: One is a setup that was never right.

choices.text: it establishes whether a warranty still applies
choices.why: Not the reason given.

prompt: What does a second user account separate?

choices.text: one program from every other program
choices.why: Not what an account boundary is.

choices.text: this machine from this network
choices.why: That needs a second machine.

choices.text: the hardware from the software
choices.why: Safe mode or a live stick does that.

choices.text: this installation from this person's settings
choices.why: One restart-free test, and a large cut.

prompt: What should be done with an error message?

choices.text: ignore it, since these messages are rarely accurate
choices.why: Somebody wrote it on purpose for this case.

choices.text: search for the first two words of it only
choices.why: The exact sentence is what finds the answer.

choices.text: record the exact words, and photograph the screen
choices.why: It is the one piece of hard evidence people discard.

choices.text: summarise it so it can be described over the phone
choices.why: The summary is what makes it worthless.

prompt: Why does the lesson dismiss "whose fault is it"?

choices.text: it narrows nothing and makes people less forthcoming
choices.why: And the person who knows what changed goes quiet.

choices.text: it is a question only a support line may ask
choices.why: Nothing about who may ask it.

choices.text: responsibility is decided after the fault is found
choices.why: True in a workplace, and not the argument.

choices.text: the answer is almost always the last person to touch it
choices.why: That is the assumption it warns against.

prompt: Why is "is it a virus" treated with suspicion?

choices.text: modern systems make a virus technically impossible
choices.why: They do not.

choices.text: viruses cannot cause the symptoms described here
choices.why: They can, and rarely do.

choices.text: nobody can test for one without special software
choices.why: You can, and that is the point.

choices.text: it is reached for when the structure has run out
choices.why: It is a hypothesis and it needs a test like any other.

prompt: Which of these count as "something changed"?

choices.text: an update that installed itself overnight
choices.why: It asks nobody and it is the commonest answer.

choices.text: the machine being a year older than last year
choices.why: Nothing happened on a particular day.

choices.text: a cable unplugged to vacuum and put back
choices.why: Put back differently, or not fully.

choices.text: the machine moved to a different room
choices.why: A different socket, a different desk, a journey.

prompt: When does a home investigation stop and a backup start?

choices.text: as soon as the next step could risk the data
choices.why: A noisy disk survives one copy, not an afternoon.

choices.text: as soon as the machine has been open for an hour
choices.why: Time is not what decides it.

choices.text: once the warranty has been confirmed as expired
choices.why: Unrelated to the risk.

choices.text: when a second person has looked at the fault
choices.why: Not a threshold for anything.

prompt: Why is the "cost more than the thing" decision hard to make?

choices.text: the price of a component is rarely known in advance
choices.why: Usually a search away.

choices.text: the hours already spent push hard the other way
choices.why: It feels like giving up rather than deciding.

choices.text: a repair is almost always cheaper than replacing
choices.why: Frequently the opposite.

choices.text: nobody can estimate how long the next step takes
choices.why: You often can, roughly.

prompt: What is wrong with recording "fixed" when you do not know why?

choices.text: a note has to name a cause if it is to be worth keeping
choices.why: Unexplained is a perfectly good entry.

choices.text: the fault was probably never fixed at all
choices.why: It may well be fixed.

choices.text: the fault returns and the note says it was dealt with
choices.why: Write unexplained, which costs nothing now.

choices.text: it is dishonest towards anybody who reads the note later
choices.why: The cost is practical rather than moral.

prompt: Which line does nobody write, and saves the most?

choices.text: the name of the person reporting it
choices.why: Already known.

choices.text: the make and the model of the machine
choices.why: Everybody writes that.

choices.text: how urgent the problem is for you
choices.why: Written constantly, and it narrows nothing.

choices.text: what you have not tried, and why

prompt: Why are the tests that PASSED worth reporting?

choices.text: each one removes a region somebody else would search
choices.why: A passed test is a result, not a non-event.

choices.text: a passing test is more reliable than a failing one is

choices.text: they show that the work was done carefully

choices.text: they are the only tests anybody can repeat

prompt: What is the line that says the remaining half is not yours?

choices.text: the point where a tool you do not own is needed
choices.why: Sometimes a stopping point, not this line.

choices.text: the point past which your changes would be on good parts

choices.text: the point where the fault has been reproduced twice

choices.text: the point at which the machine is out of warranty
choices.why: Warranty is a commercial line.

choices.text: the graphics driver is probably out of date

choices.text: the machine is old enough to be failing
